title: Risk stratification of catheter ablation of atrial fibrillation with regard to intervention-associated complications in the upper gastrointestinal tract
summary:
Atrial fibrillation is a cardiac arrhythmia. It can be treated with a procedure called interventional catheter ablation. A rare but serious complication of the procedure is the development of ulcers in the esophagus. In the most severe cases, these can lead to life-threatening connections between the heart and esophagus, with a high mortality rate.
The main aim of the study is to record how often problems develop in the esophagus after treatment for atrial fibrillation.  In addition, the corresponding clinical course will be described. Patient-dependent and intervention-dependent risk factors associated with esophageal complications will also be recorded. Secondary endpoints include recording the frequency of treatment-related gastric emptying disorders and complications of catheter ablation itself.
conditions: Atrial fibrillation and atrial flutter, unspecified

interventions.name: Retrospective inclusion of all consecutive patients after pulmonary vein isolation (PVI) of atrial fibrillation (AF) with radiofrequency ablation (RFA) on the posterior wall of the left atrium who underwent esophagogastroduodenoscopy (EGD) post-intervention.

criteria:
Inclusion criteria:
Inclusion of all patients ≥ 18 years of age who have undergone catheter ablation of atrial fibrillation at Klinikum Oldenburg AöR between 1 March 2021 and 30 April 2025
Exclusion criteria:
Exclusion of all patients < 18 years of age at the time of the intervention or who have not given written consent for ablation or post-interventional endoscopy
